mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during tightening periods.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within two months signals a weakening labor market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as economic growth prospects diminish.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during downturns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real estate sales (HOUST) by more than 5% over three months signals a weakening demand in the housing market, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and confidence wane.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during housing downturns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 2% over three months signals a strengthening supply side of the economy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings and economic growth prospects improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 60d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during expansions.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained low inflation environment (CPIAUCSL growth < 1% over 6 months) signals a stable monetary policy, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investor confidence increases.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during low inflation periods.

mechanism_narrative: A joint increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) and a decrease in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% each over two months signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as consumer spending and economic activity pick up.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases & UNRATE decreases > 0.5% each in 2 months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 5d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during labor market improvements.

mechanism_narrative: A decrease in real disposable personal income (RSAFS) by more than 2% over three months signals a weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and economic growth prospects decline.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during consumer demand downturns.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in GDP (GDPC1) by more than 3% over a quarter signals a robust economic expansion, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as corporate earnings and economic growth prospects improve.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the signal, or 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05) during expansions.
